title: Beyond Conversation: Why Documents Transform Natural Language into Code - Filip Kozera

primary.label: AI Platforms & Developer Tooling

summary: Filip Kozera, co-founder and CEO of Wordware, critiques chat-based AI interfaces and advocates document-based natural language programming as the foundation for reliable background agents. He identifies several problems with chat: context pollution from long conversations, inability to iterate structurally on artifacts, lack of forced clarity (ChatGPT doesn't always ask the right clarifying questions), poor version control, limited reusability, model laziness as context grows, absence of logical grouping or nesting, interaction with only a single abstraction layer, and critically, a concurrency of one—the user must sit and wait. Kozera positions documents as humanity's original method for specifying complex systems, citing product requirements documents dating back millennia. Documents force clarity, rigor, and structured thinking that open-ended conversation cannot. After brainstorming in chat, users should create precise documents defining what an agent should do. The talk introduces background agents activated by explicit or implicit triggers (sent emails, Slack messages, meetings with investors prompting CRM updates). These agents work asynchronously, with latency mattering less, surfacing issues only when struggling or needing approval. Kozera traces an evolution from handcrafted workflows (Zapier-style) to specialized agents with fuzzy if-else logic, to emerging general agents. For high-importance tasks, human-in-the-loop approval remains essential. He envisions organizations developing internal and external agents that communicate with each other, potentially managing humans (e.g., creating Jira tickets for engineers). He advocates a stochastic mindset—accepting agents deliver business value 99.9% of the time while focusing on ensuring the 0.1% failures aren't catastrophic. Humans will manage agent swarms, requiring taste, intent, and personal brand imbued into agents. Effective engineers today are those skilled at both IC work and managing teams of interns (AI agents). Communication protocols like MCP are early steps but need more specification around constraints, authority, and approval. Kozera predicts consumer adoption will precede slower enterprise adoption, with tools becoming the competitive moat.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

sections.title: Problems with chat-based interfaces
sections.summary: Kozera enumerates issues with chat-based AI: context pollution from long conversations, inability to iterate structurally on artifacts, lack of forced clarity, poor version control, limited reusability, model laziness as context grows, no logical grouping or nesting, and a single abstraction layer.

sections.title: Documents as the solution
sections.summary: Documents are positioned as humanity's original method for specifying complex systems, dating back millennia as product requirements documents. They force clarity and structured thinking, making them the ultimate interface for communicating complex ideas.

sections.title: Background agents and concurrency
sections.summary: Chat systems have a concurrency of one. Kozera introduces background agents, tracing evolution from handcrafted workflows (Zapier-style) to specialized agents with fuzzy if-else logic, to emerging general agents. For high-importance tasks, general agents are not yet trusted.

sections.title: Human-in-the-loop and agent communication
sections.summary: Human-in-the-loop lets users approve, reject, or fix agent outputs. Agents are triggered by explicit or implicit events (emails, Slack, meetings). Organizations will develop internal and external agents that communicate, potentially managing humans (e.g., creating Jira tickets).

sections.title: Stochastic mindset and managing agent swarms
sections.summary: Kozera advocates a stochastic mindset—accepting uncertainty when agents deliver value 99.9% of the time. Humans must manage agent swarms with taste and intent. MCP is an early communication protocol but needs more specification. Effective engineers combine IC skills with managing AI agents like teams of interns.

sections.title: Conclusion: future of the agent economy
sections.summary: After brainstorming in chat, users create structured documents defining repeatable agent processes hooked to triggers. Work becomes creating assignments, imbuing taste, and approving results (like swiping Tinder). Consumer adoption precedes enterprise; tools become the competitive moat.
